about: Ratchet vectors for the forward-secrecy ratchet (companion change A9 for the iOS port): the primitive known answers walked through one first exchange, the signed ratchet profiles, whole DM transcripts (dm) and single-frame refusals (negative) through the session layer. RatchetVectorTest rebuilds and checks them. See vectors/README.md.

deriveEpoch.note: alice's first epoch, on bob's prekey
bob's first epoch, on alice's epoch-1 key

messageNonce.note: alice's first frame (se 1, n 0, with init): boundAad = aad || headerBindingBytes(header)

spkSigningBytes.sigNote: Ed25519 by the owner's signing key; Tink's is RFC 8032 deterministic, but verify, never compare
Ed25519 by the owner's signing key; Tink's is RFC 8032 deterministic, but verify, never compare

rootTag.note: local storage only, never on the wire: the first 8 HKDF bytes, read big-endian as a signed Int64

export.note: API-only today (the spool's pairwiseRoot and a reserved sealv 2); a port may skip these

profiles.note: deliver 'sequence' in order to one fresh receiver; after each step its pin for that sender is 'expect' (prekey null = no pin). InboundPipelineTest replays it through the real pipeline.

transcriptFormat.note: dm and negative are lists of self-contained transcripts. parties: each party's identity (in identities), the signed prekeys it holds privately (profiles.prekeys names) and pins (the peer prekey it seals against). draws: every injected random value per party, in the order its engine consumes them — keyPair = X25519 priv fixtureBytes(32, seed), iv = the v2 AES-GCM IV fixtureBytes(12, seed); v3 draws no IV. steps run in order; each seal lists the draws it used (drawsUsed). A frame is a chat RelayEnvelope (recipientId = the peer) whose ChatContent.enc is encEnvelope, signed by the sender into wire. aad = aadText's bytes (MessageCrypto.header: id|sender|sentAt|recipient); v3 appends headerBindingBytes(header) and derives its nonce (kats). plaintext is MessageContent.encode() for v2 and MessageContentV2 for v3. An open uses the receiver's own now; expect is RatchetEngine.OpenOutcome's name (OPENED on success) when layer is engine, REFUSED when InboundPipeline refuses it before or around the engine; drop is the DropReason the pipeline records, and resetTriggering whether it feeds the reset heuristic; dropNormative (true everywhere but where a case says otherwise, with a dropNote) says whether a port must record that exact drop or only refuse the frame the same way. An open models the session layer only — RatchetSessions.peekOpen then commitOpen — and nothing a production receiver does around it: IntroSync's init answer, which a responder sends on first contact, is not listed. state is the actor's ratchet state for that peer after the step: secrets as sha256 hex, rootTag as the 16-hex local storage tag, skipped keys as contiguous index runs. Every step is rebuilt and checked by RatchetVectorTest; pipelineReplay cases are replayed through InboundPipeline by InboundPipelineTest, whose ratchet clock is the wall clock, so only a case whose outcome does not depend on now may set pipelineReplay.
ops: seal: actor seals contentBody to peer at now (= sentAt), against pins[peer]
open: actor opens the frame in wire (signed by peer); expect is the outcome
advance: actor seals count v3 frames of any content to peer and discards them

dm.name: firstContact
dm.note: Alice initiates to Bob's signed prekey (X3DH) and opens send epoch 1 on it (pe 0): a v2 frame, then a v3 one, both carrying the init because the session is unconfirmed. Bob, holding nothing, responds from the first frame's init and opens both; a responder's session is confirmed from the start.

dm.name: confirm
dm.note: firstContact, then Bob's first frame: his epoch 1, DHed on Alice's epoch-1 key (pe 1). Opening it confirms Alice's session (the peer sealed against an epoch of hers), so her next frame drops the init — and, her peer's base having moved past her epoch's, opens her epoch 2 on Bob's epoch 1.

dm.name: turnaround
dm.note: confirm, then the healing rule both ways: a second Alice frame stays in her epoch 2 (Bob has not moved), Bob's answer opens his epoch 2 on her epoch 2 — sealed v2, so it draws an IV — and Alice's answer to that opens her epoch 3. Every conversational turnaround is a fresh DH.

dm.name: epochCap
dm.note: MAX_EPOCH_MESSAGES = 200. firstContact leaves Alice's epoch 1 at n 2; an advance step seals n 2..197 unlisted (v3, no draws), and only the boundary frames are listed: n 198, n 199, and the next seal, which the full epoch moves to epoch 2 (still pe 0 on Bob's prekey, still with the init). Bob opens n 198 first, so n 2..197 become skipped keys, then n 199 and epoch 2's n 0.

steps.note: seal 196 v3 frames of any content and discard them: they advance the send chain from n 2 and move nothing else

dm.name: epochAge
dm.note: MAX_EPOCH_AGE_MS = 24 h, against the epoch's sendEpochStartedAt (Alice's first seal): a seal 1 ms short of it stays in epoch 1, a seal at it opens epoch 2.

dm.name: outOfOrder
dm.note: Alice seals n 0 (v2) to n 3; Bob's first frame is n 3, which establishes his session from its init and stores n 0..2 as skipped keys. n 1 and n 2 open on theirs, then n 0 (v2), and re-opening n 1 or n 3 finds the index consumed: DUPLICATE, which never triggers a reset.

negative.name: seAtCeiling
negative.note: se = MAX_EPOCH_NUMBER is in bounds: the frame reaches the key work, derives a key Alice never sealed under, and fails its AEAD — reset-triggering, unlike every out-of-bounds case

negative.name: peZeroWithoutInit
negative.note: pe 0 names our signed prekey, legal only with an init

negative.name: ekLowOrder
negative.note: an ek of small order: X25519 refuses it, and the engine reports BAD_HEADER (never a missing key)

negative.name: prekeyGone
negative.note: the init names a prekey Bob no longer holds (pruned): EPOCH_GONE, reset-triggering

negative.name: noInitNoSession
negative.note: a frame with no init (pe 1, so in bounds) to a Bob holding no session: NO_SESSION, reset-triggering

negative.name: ownEpochGone
negative.note: Bob holds the session (he opened the first frame), and a frame opens a new epoch (se 2) on an epoch of his he never minted (pe 5): EPOCH_GONE before any AEAD

negative.name: ctTampered
negative.note: the v3 frame with its last ciphertext byte flipped: every key resolves and the AEAD refuses. Nothing commits — Bob still holds no session

negative.name: initEphLowOrder
negative.note: an init whose eph is of small order. The engine does not type this: X25519 throws inside the X3DH respond, out of RatchetEngine.open, and InboundPipeline's runCatching drops it as DECRYPT_FAILED — before onRatchetFailure, so it never reaches the reset heuristic, and nothing commits

steps.dropNote: not normative: a port must refuse this frame with nothing committed and without feeding the reset heuristic, but may name the drop BAD_HEADER or DECRYPT_FAILED (Kotlin's engine throws here and the pipeline's catch records DECRYPT_FAILED)

negative.name: v3NonEmptyNonce
negative.note: a v3 envelope carries its nonce field empty (it is derived); a 12-byte one is malformed. Refused by InboundPipeline.nonceShapeValid before the engine

negative.name: v2EmptyNonce
negative.note: the mirror: a v2 envelope carries a 12-byte IV, so an empty one is malformed (nonceShapeValid)

negative.name: v3ToGroup
negative.note: v3 is the DM form by rule: Alice's v3 frame re-addressed to the group of alice, bob and carol (recipientId absent) routes to the DM arm and is refused there, before any group or reset logic. The receiver holds the group (its members are in groupMembers)
